children: Banks across the country will be closed today, September 11, as the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) goes ahead with its nationwide strike. The strike is over long-pending demands for a five-day banking week, changes to the new Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme and pension-related issues.
No Concrete Development Rather than "As Soon As possible " from Government side on 5 Days Banking, Strike stands March on
— United Forum of Bank Unions (@UFBUIndia) September 10, 2026
Public sector banks are expected to be hit hardest, while private and foreign banks may see partial disruption.

Branch services such as cash deposits and withdrawals, cheque clearance and loan processing could be slow or unavailable at affected branches. ATMs, UPI, net banking and mobile banking are expected to continue functioning as normal, barring scheduled maintenance or other service disruptions.
State Bank of India (SBI) and Union Bank of India have cautioned customers that banking operations could be affected due to the strike.
As September 11 is a Friday, followed by the weekend and the Ganesh Chaturthi holiday in some states on September 14, customers in those states could face up to four consecutive days of disruption.

This is the first in a planned series of strikes. UFBU has also planned further strikes for September 28, 29 and 30, followed by a continuous strike from October 26 if the demands are not met. While banks have reassured customers that they will make arrangements to minimise disruptions, branch-level services could still be affected.

title: Bank strike today: Will branches be open? Here’s what we know
